title: The Erdős-Pósa property for prime-length cycles fails (and beyond)
summary: We prove that for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$, prime-length cycles do not have the $\frac{1}{t}$-integral Erdős-Pósa property, even when restricted to planar graphs. We in fact prove a more general density result. For every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subset $L \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with lower density zero, the set of cycles whose length is in $L$ do not have the $\frac{1}{t}$-integral Erdős-Pósa property, even when restricted to planar graphs.
